projects.name: Budera AI Legion
projects.label: Built as CTO · 2025
projects.tagline: An AI business partner: five built-in agents plus ones you build, working from your real Stripe, Shopify and Analytics data.
projects.stack: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Postgres, Drizzle ORM, OpenAI-compatible LLMs, Stripe, Shopify, Google Analytics, Vitest
projects.details:
Budera is an AI business partner for founders. Five built-in agents study a company, its market and its competitors, and owners build their own agents for anything else. Every agent returns a short brief and tasks that land in one list.

- A provider-neutral agent engine that runs on any OpenAI-compatible model, with its own research tool loop and validated structured output
- Live web search and a safe page reader, so research agents cite real sources
- Stripe, Shopify and Google Analytics connections with encrypted secrets, so reports use real revenue, orders and traffic
- Owner-built agents with templates, tools and daily or weekly schedules
- Several companies per account, and a live demo workspace with sample data

projects.name: Dimtse · ድምፄ
projects.label: Nonprofit · Assistive tech
projects.tagline: A free talk board for non-verbal children, driven by their eyes or head through a webcam or phone. Amharic and English, built for children with cerebral palsy in Ethiopia.
projects.stack: MediaPipe face landmarker in the browser, ridge-regression calibration, vanilla JS, Python server, Docker, GitHub Actions, edge-tts
projects.details:
Commercial eye-gaze communication devices cost thousands of dollars and don't speak Amharic. Dimtse runs on hardware a family already owns and costs nothing. By Happy Lucky Chacho, Bahir Dar.

- **Three big choices at a time.** Look at one and hold your gaze; it fills up, then speaks. Fourteen pages that wrap around, so there is never a dead end, plus story time and a spelling keyboard that never shows more than six things
- **Eyes, head, or both.** Head pose is measured far more precisely than eye direction, so a child who can't hold their eyes steady can point with their head. Each mode has its own calibration, and the board stops guessing when tracking can't be trusted
- **Every child has their own board.** A carer puts a photo of the real person or thing on a tile, records each phrase in their own voice (almost no device has an Amharic voice), adds pages, and writes follow-up questions: "It hurts" leads to *Where?*
- **Tracking runs in the browser.** Google's MediaPipe face landmarker, vendored so nothing leaves the device. The server only serves files and stores boards, so the board works offline and can be added to a phone's home screen
- **The guide is part of the app.** A plain-language guide for the person sitting next to the child: light, first sessions built on delight, modelling, waiting, and a first-month plan

Status: a working prototype, not yet trialled with children. Nearly every design decision came from measuring a failure, and the code comments record which.

projects.name: Agent setups for teams
projects.label: Service · Claude Code, Codex, Grok
projects.tagline: I set up Claude Code, Codex and Grok bots inside a team's own systems: their repos, docs, CRM and chat, with the access and guardrails each one needs.
projects.stack: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Grok, MCP, GitHub, Slack, Telegram
projects.details:
Most teams already pay for an AI model. What they're missing is the wiring that lets it do real work inside their own tools. I do that wiring.

- **Claude Code and Codex** in a team's repositories, with project instructions, custom agents and slash commands, hooks, and CI checks, so the coding agent follows the team's rules
- **MCP servers** that give agents safe, scoped access to the company's database, docs, CRM, tickets and calendars
- **Grok and other chat bots** in Telegram, Slack and WhatsApp, answering from company knowledge and handing off to a person when they should
- **Scheduled agents** for reports, research, lead lists and follow-ups, running on a server rather than someone's laptop
- **Guardrails**: separate keys per agent, read-only access by default, approval before anything is sent or spent, and logs of what each agent did
- **Handover**: a short written runbook and a session with the team, so they can change the setup themselves

I've done this for my own companies and for clients in the US, Australia and Ethiopia.

projects.name: OpenClaw agents
projects.label: Private · 15 agents
projects.tagline: Fifteen agents on OpenClaw that research, audit, write and draft outreach. Many drive a real Chrome window the way a person would.
projects.stack: OpenClaw, Python, Playwright, PyAutoGUI, OpenCV, Google Workspace APIs, Stripe, WordPress, ReportLab, Whisper, Ollama
projects.details:
OpenClaw runs my personal agent workspace. On top of it I built a browser layer, "agent as human" mode: it drives a real Chrome window with screenshots, OCR and on-screen matching, so an agent can use sites that have no API. Most of the agents below run on a schedule and deliver to Google Docs, Sheets, Gmail drafts, WordPress or Telegram.

1. **SEO audit**: audits a site and writes a 15-page PDF report, sent to Telegram
2. **Reputation repair**: finds restaurants with weak reviews, makes a report card for each, and drafts the pitch email. Runs weekly, one city at a time
3. **Content Cannon**: writes three SEO articles every morning, publishes them to WordPress, drafts the social posts and logs everything to a sheet
4. **Amazon product research**: reads best-seller lists and turns the findings into an article in Google Docs
5. **Ad spy**: checks which local service businesses run Google Ads and how their landing pages hold up
6. **Legal lead finder**: checks law firms' blogs, Google Business profiles, mobile sites and ads, then fills a lead sheet and drafts emails. Runs weekly
7. **Store spy**: finds Shopify stores in a niche, reads their products and compares AliExpress prices for a margin report
8. **Real estate content**: turns new listings into blog posts and Instagram scripts, posted to WordPress
9. **Course marketing**: reads a course's sales page, studies competing courses and writes the full launch package
10. **YouTube research**: studies what's trending in a niche and why, and emails a weekly PDF
11. **Churn preventer**: reads Stripe, flags customers likely to cancel, and drafts personal retention emails in Gmail
12. **Expired domains**: finds and ranks expired domains in a niche, with a PDF valuation
13. **Podcast guest booker**: finds mid-size podcasts, reads recent episodes, finds the host and drafts a pitch
14. **Client reports**: pulls each client's analytics, rankings, social and reviews every month, and sends a branded PDF
15. **Personal assistant**: calendar, voice-note transcription, daily stand-ups and project tracking, with local models through Ollama

The repository is private. I can walk you through it on a call.
